enc.title: Sheet 1 Q1: Compton effect

source.where: Exercise sheet I, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 1.pdf

enc.goal: (i) Thomson: an electron at rest in the field $\vec E=\vec\varepsilon E_0\cos(kx-\omega t)$ obeys $m\ddot{\vec x}=-e\vec E$ (magnetic force neglected). Solve it; what is the frequency of the emitted light? (ii) Compton: treat light as photons, $(cp_1,\vec p_1)$, $\lambda_1=h/p_1$, scattering elastically off the electron by an angle $\theta$. Show $\lambda_2=\lambda_1+\frac{h}{mc}(1-\cos\theta)$. (iii) In which limit is Thomson scattering recovered, and for which light is the Compton effect observable?

steps.reveal: With $\vec k\parallel\hat e_3$ the motion is transverse: $\vec x(t)=-\frac{eE_0}{m\omega^2}\vec\varepsilon(1-\cos\omega t)$. The electron oscillates at $\omega$ and radiates as a dipole at the same frequency $\omega$: no frequency shift classically.

$(cp_1,\vec p_1)+(mc^2,0)=(cp_2,\vec p_2)+(\sqrt{m^2c^4+p^2c^2},\vec p)$. Eliminate the electron: $p^2=p_1^2-2p_1p_2\cos\theta+p_2^2$ (momentum), and from the energy $(p_1-p_2+mc)^2=m^2c^2+p^2$. Together $2p_1p_2(1-\cos\theta)=2mc(p_1-p_2)$; divide by $p_1p_2$ and use $\lambda=h/p$.

The shift is at most $2h/mc$ with $\lambda_C=h/mc=2.42\times10^{-12}$ m. For $\lambda\gg\lambda_C$ (visible light, $10^{-7}$ m) the relative change is negligible: Thomson. Only hard X-rays and $\gamma$-rays show it.

enc.title: Sheet 1 Q2: Bohr atom

source.where: Exercise sheet I, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 1.pdf

enc.goal: Bohr: $mv_nr_n=n\hbar$, $r_n=\frac{n^2\hbar^2}{me^2}$ (Gaussian units). (i) With $\lambda=h/p$ show $\lambda/r_n=2\pi/n$: the wave fits around the orbit. (ii) Show $v_n\ll c$. (iii) Show that the emitted wavelength (e.g. $n=\infty\to1$) is much larger than the Bohr radius.

steps.reveal: $\frac{\lambda}{r_n}=\frac{h}{mv_nr_n}=\frac{2\pi\hbar}{n\hbar}=\frac{2\pi}n$: $n$ wavelengths fit on the circumference.
$v_n=\frac{n\hbar}{mr_n}=\frac{e^2}{n\hbar}\le v_1=\alpha c=2.19\times10^6$ m/s $\ll c$ ($\alpha\approx1/137$).

$E_n=-13.6\ \mathrm{eV}/n^2$, $\lambda_{nm}=\frac{hc}{E_n-E_m}\ge\lambda_{\infty1}=\frac{hc}{13.6\ \mathrm{eV}}\approx91$ nm $\gg a_0=0.053$ nm: the atom is tiny compared with its light (dipole approximation).

questions.title: Galilei invariance of the Schrödinger equation

enc.title: Sheet 1 Q3: Galilei invariance of the Schrödinger equation

source.where: Exercise sheet I, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 1.pdf

enc.goal: If $\Psi(x,t)$ solves the free Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\partial_t\Psi=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\partial_x^2\Psi$, show that $\Psi_u(x,t)=\Psi(x-ut,t)\exp\left[\frac{im}{\hbar}ux-\frac{im}{2\hbar}u^2t\right]$ is a solution for every constant $u$.

steps.reveal: $i\hbar\partial_t\Psi_u=\left[i\hbar\partial_t\Psi-i\hbar u\,\partial_x\Psi+\frac m2u^2\Psi\right]e^{imu(x-ut/2)/\hbar}$ (arguments $x-ut,t$), and $i\hbar\partial_t\Psi=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\partial_x^2\Psi$.

$-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\partial_x^2\Psi_u=\left[-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\partial_x^2\Psi-i\hbar u\,\partial_x\Psi+\frac m2u^2\Psi\right]e^{imu(x-ut/2)/\hbar}$: identical. The phase $e^{imux/\hbar}$ is the boost of the momentum by $mu$.

keyPoints: both sides give the same three terms

enc.title: Sheet 2 Q1: Ehrenfest’s theorem

source.where: Exercise sheet II, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 2.pdf

enc.goal: Prove $m\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\langle x\rangle=-\langle V^\prime(x)\rangle$ for motion in a potential $V$. Hint: bring $\frac{d}{dt}\langle x\rangle$ into a form proportional to $\Psi\overleftrightarrow{\partial_x}\Psi^*$.

steps.reveal: With the Schrödinger equation, $\frac{d}{dt}\langle x\rangle=\frac{i\hbar}{2m}\int x\,\partial_x(\Psi^*\partial_x\Psi-\Psi\partial_x\Psi^*)dx=-\frac{i\hbar}{2m}\int(\Psi^*\partial_x\Psi-\Psi\partial_x\Psi^*)dx=\frac{\langle p\rangle}{m}$ (integration by parts, no boundary terms).

$\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\langle x\rangle=\frac1m\int\left[(H\Psi)^*\partial_x\Psi+\partial_x\Psi^*(H\Psi)\right]dx$; the kinetic terms cancel by parts, the potential terms give $\int\left[\Psi^*V\partial_x\Psi+\partial_x\Psi^*V\Psi\right]=-\int\Psi^*(\partial_xV)\Psi$.
$m\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\langle x\rangle=-\langle\partial_xV\rangle$: Newton for averages. Not $-V^\prime(\langle x\rangle)$, except for at most quadratic $V$.

enc.title: Sheet 2 Q2: Reality of energy

source.where: Exercise sheet II, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 2.pdf

enc.goal: Show that the expectation value of the Hamiltonian of a non-relativistic particle is real, $\langle H\rangle=\langle H\rangle^*$.

steps.reveal: $\langle H\rangle=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\int\Psi^*\Psi^{\prime\prime}+\langle V\rangle$, $\langle H\rangle^*=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\int\Psi^{*\prime\prime}\Psi+\langle V\rangle$ ($V$ real).
$\int(\Psi^*\Psi^{\prime\prime}-\Psi^{*\prime\prime}\Psi)=\int(-\Psi^{*\prime}\Psi^\prime+\Psi^{*\prime}\Psi^\prime)=0$ by parts: $H$ is hermitian on normalisable states.

enc.title: Sheet 2 Q3: Probability current

source.where: Exercise sheet II, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 2.pdf

enc.goal: Show that $\Psi_k=\left(Ae^{ikx/\hbar}+Be^{-ikx/\hbar}\right)e^{-iE_kt/\hbar}$, $E_k=k^2/2m$, solves the free Schrödinger equation and that its current is $j=\frac km(|A|^2-|B|^2)$.

steps.reveal: Each $e^{\pm ikx/\hbar}e^{-iE_kt/\hbar}$ solves it ($i\hbar\cdot(-iE_k/\hbar)=\frac{k^2}{2m}$), the time factor is even in $k$, and the equation is linear.

$j=\frac{\hbar}{2mi}(\Psi^*\partial_x\Psi-\Psi\partial_x\Psi^*)$: the cross terms $AB^*$ cancel, leaving $\frac km(|A|^2-|B|^2)$: right-movers minus left-movers, each with velocity $k/m$ ($k$ is the momentum here).

enc.title: Sheet 3 Q1: Gaussian wave functions

source.where: Exercise sheet III, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 3.pdf

enc.goal: $\Psi(x)=Ae^{-\lambda x^2/2}$, $\lambda>0$. (i) Normalise. (ii) Sketch; find $V$ (with $V(0)=0$) for which $\Psi$ is a stationary state, and $E$. (iii) Compute $\Delta x$, $\Delta p$ and $\Delta x\Delta p$. (iv) How would you tune $\lambda$ to localise the particle, and why can $\Delta x=0$ not be reached?

steps.reveal: $\int|A|^2e^{-\lambda x^2}dx=|A|^2\sqrt{\pi/\lambda}=1$: $A=(\lambda/\pi)^{1/4}$ (up to a phase).

$\Psi^{\prime\prime}=(\lambda^2x^2-\lambda)\Psi$, so $V=\frac{\hbar^2\lambda^2}{2m}x^2$ and $E=\frac{\hbar^2\lambda}{2m}$: the harmonic oscillator ground state ($\lambda=m\omega/\hbar$, $E=\hbar\omega/2$). Larger $\lambda$: narrower bell.

$\langle x\rangle=\langle p\rangle=0$, $\langle x^2\rangle=\frac1{2\lambda}$ (differentiate $\int e^{-\lambda x^2}$ w.r.t. $\lambda$), $\langle p^2\rangle=\frac{\hbar^2\lambda}2$: $\Delta x\Delta p=\frac\hbar2$, the minimum.
Large $\lambda$ (steep trap) gives small $\Delta x$, but $\Delta p=\hbar\sqrt{\lambda/2}$ and $E=\hbar^2\lambda/2m$ diverge: $\Delta x\to0$ costs infinite energy.

enc.title: Sheet 3 Q2: Particle in a box I

source.where: Exercise sheet III, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 3.pdf

enc.goal: (i) A particle in $[0,a]$ has $\Psi(x,0)=1/\sqrt a$. Probability of measuring $E_n=\frac{n^2\pi^2\hbar^2}{2ma^2}$? ($\psi_n=\sqrt{2/a}\sin\frac{n\pi x}a$.) (ii) Deduce $\sum_m\frac1{(2m-1)^2}=\frac{\pi^2}8$ and $\zeta(2)=\frac{\pi^2}6$.

steps.reveal: $p_n=\left|\int_0^a\sqrt{\frac2a}\sin\frac{n\pi x}{a}\frac{1}{\sqrt a}dx\right|^2=\frac{2}{n^2\pi^2}(1-(-1)^n)^2=\frac{8}{n^2\pi^2}$ for odd $n$, 0 for even $n$.
$\sum p_n=1\Rightarrow\sum_{\rm odd}\frac1{n^2}=\frac{\pi^2}8$. Then $\zeta(2)=\frac{\zeta(2)}4+\frac{\pi^2}8$, so $\zeta(2)=\frac{\pi^2}6$.

enc.title: Sheet 3 Q3: Particle in a box II

source.where: Exercise sheet III, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 3.pdf

enc.goal: In the $n$-th eigenstate of the box $[0,a]$ show $\langle x\rangle=\frac a2$, $\langle(x-\langle x\rangle)^2\rangle=\frac{a^2}{12}\left(1-\frac{6}{n^2\pi^2}\right)$, and that the classical limit is approached as $n\to\infty$.

steps.reveal: $\langle x\rangle=\int_0^a\frac{x}{a}\left(1-\cos\frac{2\pi nx}a\right)dx=\frac a2$ (the cosine term integrates to 0 by parts).
$\langle x^2\rangle=\frac{a^2}3-\frac{a^2}{2\pi^2n^2}$ (two integrations by parts), so $(\Delta x)^2=\frac{a^2}{12}-\frac{a^2}{2\pi^2n^2}$.
A classical particle is uniform on $[0,a]$: $\langle x\rangle=a/2$, $(\Delta x)^2=a^2/12$, reached for $n\to\infty$ (correspondence principle).

keyPoints: uniform classical distribution as the limit

questions.title: Particle in a box III: the sudden wall

enc.title: Sheet 3 Q4: Particle in a box III: the sudden wall

source.where: Exercise sheet III, Question 4; official solution: Solutions 3.pdf

enc.goal: A particle in the ground state of $[0,a]$; the wall at $a$ jumps suddenly to $2a$. Expand in the eigenfunctions of $[0,2a]$, give $\Psi(x,t)$, show that only $n=2$ and odd $n$ contribute ($E_n=\frac{n^2\pi^2\hbar^2}{8ma^2}$) and that the energy is unchanged with probability 1/2. Classical intuition?

steps.reveal: $c_n=\frac{\sqrt2}{a}\int_0^a\sin\frac{\pi x}a\sin\frac{n\pi x}{2a}dx$; with $2\sin\sin=\cos-\cos$: $c_2=\frac1{\sqrt2}$, and for $n\ne2$: $c_n=\frac{\sin\pi(1-n/2)}{\sqrt2\pi(1-n/2)}-\frac{\sin\pi(1+n/2)}{\sqrt2\pi(1+n/2)}$, zero for even $n>2$.
$\Psi(x,t)=\sum c_n\psi_n(x)e^{-iE_nt/\hbar}$. $E_2$ of the new box equals the old ground energy: probability $|c_2|^2=\frac12$ (odd $n$: $P_n=\frac{32}{\pi^2(4-n^2)^2}$).

The particle bounces freely; moving a wall instantly (not touching it) does not change its kinetic energy. Quantum mechanically the mean energy is conserved too ($\langle H\rangle$ of the unchanged state), but individual outcomes spread.

enc.title: Sheet 4 Q1: One-dimensional delta potential

source.where: Exercise sheet IV, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 4.pdf

enc.goal: $V=V\delta(x)$; ansatz $\psi=e^{ikx/\hbar}+Re^{-ikx/\hbar}$ ($x<0$), $Te^{ikx/\hbar}$ ($x>0$), $E=k^2/2m$. Find the matching conditions, $R$, $T$ and check $|R|^2+|T|^2=1$.

steps.reveal: Integrate from $-\epsilon$ to $\epsilon$: $\psi$ continuous, $\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}(\psi^\prime(0^+)-\psi^\prime(0^-))=V\psi(0)$.
$1+R=T$ and $\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\frac{ik}{\hbar}(T-1+R)=VT$ give $R=\frac{-imV}{\hbar k+imV}$, $T=\frac{\hbar k}{\hbar k+imV}$.
$|R|^2+|T|^2=\frac{m^2V^2+\hbar^2k^2}{\hbar^2k^2+m^2V^2}=1$. High energies transmit, the sign of $V$ does not matter for $|T|$.

enc.title: Sheet 4 Q2: Infinitely deep, infinitely narrow well

source.where: Exercise sheet IV, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 4.pdf

enc.goal: Square well $V=-V_0$ for $|x|<a$. Show that for $V_0\to\infty$, $a\to0$ with $V_0a$ fixed the ground-state energy stays finite and negative.

steps.reveal: $\psi=b\cos kx$ inside, $e^{-\kappa|x|}$ outside, $k=\sqrt{2m(E+V_0)}/\hbar$, $\kappa=\sqrt{-2mE}/\hbar$; matching: $e^{-\kappa a}=b\cos ka$, $\kappa e^{-\kappa a}=bk\sin ka$.
$ka\to0$ (since $k\sim\sqrt{V_0}$, $a\sim1/V_0$): $b=1$, $\kappa=k^2a\to\frac{2mV_0a}{\hbar^2}$, so $E_0=-\frac{\hbar^2\kappa^2}{2m}=-\frac{2m(V_0a)^2}{\hbar^2}$, finite.
The well becomes $-2V_0a\,\delta(x)$; with the jump condition of Q1, $\psi=e^{-\kappa|x|}$ gives the same $\kappa$. Exactly one bound state.

enc.title: Sheet 4 Q3: General potentials

source.where: Exercise sheet IV, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 4.pdf

enc.goal: (i) For a stationary scattering state $\chi=e^{ikx}+Ae^{-ikx}$ ($x\ll0$), $Be^{ikx}$ ($x\gg0$) show that $j$ is independent of $x$ and $|A|^2+|B|^2=1$; interpret. (ii) Show $\langle T\rangle\ge0$ and that the lowest energy in any well lies above the bottom of the well.

steps.reveal: $\partial_xj=-\partial_t|\psi|^2=0$ for stationary states. Left: $j=\frac{\hbar k}m(1-|A|^2)$, right: $\frac{\hbar k}m|B|^2$: equal, so $|A|^2+|B|^2=1$: every particle is reflected or transmitted.
$\langle T\rangle=\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\int|\partial_x\psi|^2\ge0$ (by parts), strictly $>0$ for a normalisable state. Hence $\langle H\rangle\ge V_{\min}+\langle T\rangle>V_{\min}$.

enc.title: Sheet 4 Q4: The deuteron

source.where: Exercise sheet IV, Question 4; official solution: Solutions 4.pdf

enc.goal: 3D square well $V=-V$ for $r<a$, 0 outside. Find the spherically symmetric bound states (hint: $\chi=r\psi$). Is there always a bound state?

steps.reveal: $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\chi^{\prime\prime}+V(r)\chi=E\chi$ with $\chi(0)=0$: the 1D well, but only odd solutions.
$\chi=\sin kr$ inside, $e^{-\kappa r}$ outside; with $\xi=ka$, $\eta=\kappa a$: $\eta=-\xi\cot\xi$ and $\xi^2+\eta^2=\frac{2ma^2V}{\hbar^2}$.
$-\xi\cot\xi<0$ for $\xi<\pi/2$, so a solution needs $\frac{2ma^2V}{\hbar^2}>\frac{\pi^2}4$: unlike 1D, a 3D well needs a minimum depth $V>\frac{\pi^2\hbar^2}{8ma^2}$. The deuteron is barely bound.

enc.title: Sheet 5 Q1: Transfer matrix method

source.where: Exercise sheet V, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 5.pdf

enc.goal: Piecewise constant potentials. (i) Step $V_L\to V_R$ at 0: find $M$ with $\binom{A_L}{B_L}=M\binom{A_R}{B_R}$. (ii) Propagation matrix $N$ over a region $[x_1,x_2]$. (iii) Chain them for a general potential. (iv) Square well $-V$ for $|x|<\ell/2$: $M_{\rm full}$; when is $N=I$, and what does it mean? (v) Barrier $V$, $0<E<V$, $B_R=0$, $A_L=1$: show $|B_L|^2+|A_R|^2=1$ and compute $|A_R|^2$.

steps.reveal: Continuity of $\psi,\psi^\prime$: $A_L+B_L=A_R+B_R$, $k(A_L-B_L)=q(A_R-B_R)$, so $M=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1+\eta&1-\eta\\1-\eta&1+\eta\end{pmatrix}$, $\eta=q/k$.
$N=\mathrm{diag}(e^{-ik\ell},e^{ik\ell})$, $\ell=x_2-x_1$. In general $\binom{A_L}{B_L}=M_{n+1,n}N_nM_{n,n-1}\cdots N_1M_{1,0}\binom{A_R}{B_R}$.
$M_{\rm full}=M^{-1}NM$ with $q=\sqrt{2m(E+V)}/\hbar$. $N=I$ iff $q\ell=2\pi n$: the wave fits into the well, $M_{\rm full}=I$, perfect transmission (resonance).

$q=i\kappa$, $\alpha=k/\kappa$: $1=A_R(\cosh\kappa\ell+\frac i2\frac{1-\alpha^2}{\alpha}\sinh\kappa\ell)$, $B_L=A_R\frac i2\frac{1+\alpha^2}\alpha\sinh\kappa\ell$; squaring gives $|A_R|^2+|B_L|^2=1$ and $T=|A_R|^2=\left[1+\frac{V^2}{4E(V-E)}\sinh^2\kappa\ell\right]^{-1}$. Classically $T=0$.

enc.title: Sheet 5 Q2: Rays in $\mathbb C^2$

source.where: Exercise sheet V, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 5.pdf

enc.goal: $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$ with basis $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$. (i) Are $|\Psi\rangle$ and $\mu|\Psi\rangle$ physically different? (ii) Show almost every state is $|1\rangle+z|2\rangle$; which are not, and do different $z$ give different states? (iii) What state is $|z|\to\infty$? (iv) What geometric object is the space of states?

steps.reveal: All probabilities $\frac{|\langle\Phi|\Psi\rangle|^2}{\langle\Phi|\Phi\rangle\langle\Psi|\Psi\rangle}$ are unchanged by $\mu$: physical states are rays.
$a|1\rangle+b|2\rangle\sim|1\rangle+\frac ba|2\rangle$ if $a\ne0$; distinct $z$ are distinct rays. Only $|2\rangle$ is missing, and it is the limit $|z|\to\infty$.
$\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$ is the Riemann sphere $S^2$ (stereographic projection): the Bloch sphere of a spin-$\frac12$/qubit, $\mathbb{CP}^1\cong S^2$.

enc.title: Sheet 5 Q3: Commutators

source.where: Exercise sheet V, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 5.pdf

enc.goal: (i) Show $(iAB)^\dagger=-iB^\dagger A^\dagger$ and that $i[A,B]$ is self-adjoint for self-adjoint $A,B$. (ii) With $[x,p]=i\hbar$ show $e^{iap/\hbar}xe^{-iap/\hbar}=x+a$. (iii) Deduce $e^{iap/\hbar}f(x)e^{-iap/\hbar}=f(x+a)$ and Weyl’s relation $e^{iap/\hbar}e^{ibx/\hbar}=e^{iba/\hbar}e^{ibx/\hbar}e^{iap/\hbar}$.

steps.reveal: $\langle f|iABg\rangle=\langle-iB^\dagger A^\dagger f|g\rangle$ for all $f,g$. Then $(i[A,B])^\dagger=-iBA+iAB=i[A,B]$.
$p^nx=xp^n-ni\hbar p^{n-1}$, so $e^{iap/\hbar}x=(x+a)e^{iap/\hbar}$; multiply by $e^{-iap/\hbar}$ from the right ($e^{iap/\hbar}e^{-iap/\hbar}=I$).
Conjugation is multiplicative, so $x^n\to(x+a)^n$ and $f(x)\to f(x+a)$. With $f=e^{ibx/\hbar}$: $e^{iap/\hbar}e^{ibx/\hbar}=e^{ib(x+a)/\hbar}e^{iap/\hbar}$, the Weyl form.

enc.title: Sheet 6 Q1: Delta well in momentum space

source.where: Exercise sheet VI, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 6.pdf

enc.goal: $V=-\alpha\delta(x)$. (i) Bound states in position space. (ii) Show the momentum-space equation $\frac{p^2}{2m}\tilde\psi+\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi\hbar}}\int\tilde V(p-p^\prime)\tilde\psi(p^\prime)dp^\prime=E\tilde\psi$. (iii) Compute $\tilde V$ and solve in terms of $C=\int\tilde\psi\,dp$. (iv) Get the allowed $E$. (v) Compare with the Fourier transform of (i). (vi) What goes wrong for $E>0$, or for a barrier?

steps.reveal: $\psi=Ae^{-\kappa|x|}$, jump $\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}(\psi^\prime(0^+)-\psi^\prime(0^-))=-\alpha\psi(0)$ gives $\kappa=\frac{m\alpha}{\hbar^2}$, one bound state $E=-\frac{m\alpha^2}{2\hbar^2}$.

Fourier transforming, $V\psi$ becomes a convolution; $\tilde V=-\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{2\pi\hbar}}$ is constant, so the integral term is $-\frac{\alpha C}{2\pi\hbar}$ and $\left(\frac{p^2}{2m}-E\right)\tilde\psi=\frac{\alpha C}{2\pi\hbar}$: $\tilde\psi(p)=\frac{\alpha C}{2\pi\hbar}\,\frac{1}{p^2/2m-E}$, with $C=\sqrt{2\pi\hbar}\,\psi(0)$.

Integrating both sides: $C=\frac{m\alpha C}{\hbar\sqrt{-2mE}}$, so $\hbar\sqrt{-2mE}=m\alpha$: the same $E$. The transform of $e^{-\kappa|x|}$ is a Lorentzian $\propto\frac{2\kappa}{\kappa^2+p^2/\hbar^2}$: the same function.
$E>0$: poles at $p=\pm\sqrt{2mE}$, $C$ diverges (scattering states are not normalisable). Barrier $+\alpha^\prime\delta$: $-m\alpha^\prime=\hbar\sqrt{-2mE}>0$ is impossible: no bound state.

enc.title: Sheet 6 Q2: Uncertainty relation in a box

source.where: Exercise sheet VI, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 6.pdf

enc.goal: For the $n$-th eigenstate of the box $[0,a]$ ($\langle x\rangle=a/2$, $(\Delta x)^2=\frac{a^2}{12}(1-\frac6{n^2\pi^2})$, sheet III) compute $\langle p\rangle$, $\Delta p$ and check $\Delta x\Delta p\ge\hbar/2$.

steps.reveal: $\langle p\rangle=0$ (the integrand $\sin\cos$ is odd about $a/2$), $\langle p^2\rangle=\left(\frac{n\pi\hbar}a\right)^2$ (also $=2mE_n$), so $\Delta p=\frac{n\pi\hbar}a$.
$\Delta x\Delta p=\frac\hbar2\sqrt{\frac{n^2\pi^2}3-2}\ge\frac\hbar2\times1.13$ for $n=1$, growing with $n$: Heisenberg holds, not saturated.

enc.title: Sheet 6 Q3: Uncertainty relation and energy

source.where: Exercise sheet VI, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 6.pdf

enc.goal: $V=\frac12kx^2$. Express $\langle E\rangle$ through $\langle x\rangle,\langle p\rangle,\Delta x,\Delta p$, and use $\Delta x\Delta p\ge\hbar/2$ to show $\langle E\rangle\ge\frac\hbar2\sqrt{k/m}$.

steps.reveal: $\langle E\rangle=\frac{(\Delta p)^2+\langle p\rangle^2}{2m}+\frac k2\left((\Delta x)^2+\langle x\rangle^2\right)\ge\frac{(\Delta p)^2}{2m}+\frac k2(\Delta x)^2$.

Complete the square: $\ge\sqrt{k/m}\,\Delta x\Delta p\ge\frac\hbar2\sqrt{k/m}=\frac{\hbar\omega}2$ (or minimise $\frac{\mu}{2m}+\frac{k\hbar^2}{8\mu}$ over $\mu=(\Delta p)^2$). The zero-point energy is forced by uncertainty, and it is exactly the true ground state.

keyPoints: expectation values split into mean$^2$ + variance

enc.title: Sheet 7 Q1: 2D harmonic oscillator

source.where: Exercise sheet VII, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 7.pdf

enc.goal: $H=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\left(-\partial_x^2-\partial_y^2+x^2+y^2\right)$ (dimensionless coordinates). (i) Introduce $a,a^\dagger,b,b^\dagger$ and show $H=\hbar\omega(a^\dagger a+b^\dagger b+1)$; give their commutators. (ii) Find the eigenstates and the vacuum wave function $\psi_0(x,y)$. (iii) Show that $H$ is invariant under $\binom{a}{b}\to R(\varphi)\binom{a}{b}$, $R=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\varphi&-\sin\varphi\\ \sin\varphi&\cos\varphi\end{pmatrix}$ (same on $a^\dagger,b^\dagger$); what does it do to $x,y$? (iv) Find the generator $J$: $[J,a]=\frac{d}{d\varphi}a(\varphi)|_0$, $[J,b]=\frac{d}{d\varphi}b(\varphi)|_0$. (v) Show $[H,J]=0$ and diagonalise $J$ on the states with $E\le2\hbar\omega$.

steps.reveal: $a=\frac1{\sqrt2}(x+\partial_x)$, $a^\dagger=\frac1{\sqrt2}(x-\partial_x)$, same for $b$ with $y$. $[a,a^\dagger]=[b,b^\dagger]=1$, all other commutators vanish. $a^\dagger a=\frac12(x^2-1-\partial_x^2)$, hence $H=\hbar\omega(a^\dagger a+b^\dagger b+1)$.

$|m,n\rangle=\frac{(a^\dagger)^m(b^\dagger)^n}{\sqrt{m!\,n!}}|0,0\rangle$, $E=\hbar\omega(m+n+1)$ (degeneracy $N+1$ at $E=\hbar\omega(N+1)$). $a|0\rangle=b|0\rangle=0$ gives $(x+\partial_x)\psi_0=(y+\partial_y)\psi_0=0$: $\psi_0=\pi^{-1/2}e^{-(x^2+y^2)/2}$.

$H=\hbar\omega\,(a^\dagger\ b^\dagger)\binom ab+\hbar\omega$ and $R^TR=I$, so $H$ is invariant. Since $x=(a+a^\dagger)/\sqrt2$, $y=(b+b^\dagger)/\sqrt2$, $x,y$ are rotated by the same $R(\varphi)$: rotational symmetry of the isotropic oscillator.

$\frac{d}{d\varphi}a(\varphi)|_0=-b$, $\frac{d}{d\varphi}b(\varphi)|_0=a$; $J=a^\dagger b-b^\dagger a$ does it ($[a^\dagger b,a]=-b$, $[-b^\dagger a,b]=a$). $iJ$ is (up to $\hbar$) the angular momentum $L_z$.

$[H,a^\dagger b]=a^\dagger(-\hbar\omega b)+\hbar\omega a^\dagger b=0$, same for $b^\dagger a$. $J|m,n\rangle=\sqrt{(m+1)n}|m+1,n-1\rangle-\sqrt{m(n+1)}|m-1,n+1\rangle$. On $\{|0,0\rangle,|1,0\rangle,|0,1\rangle\}$: $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0\\0&0&1\\0&-1&0\end{pmatrix}$, eigenvectors $|0,0\rangle$ (0), $\frac1{\sqrt2}(|1,0\rangle\pm i|0,1\rangle)$ ($\pm i$).

enc.title: Sheet 7 Q2: Coherent states

source.where: Exercise sheet VII, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 7.pdf

enc.goal: $a|\alpha\rangle=\alpha|\alpha\rangle$, $\langle\alpha|\alpha\rangle=1$. (i) Show $|\alpha\rangle=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}e^{\alpha a^\dagger}|0\rangle$. (ii) Show $|\alpha\rangle(t)=e^{-i\omega t/2}|\alpha e^{-i\omega t}\rangle$. (iii) Compute $\langle x\rangle(t)$, $\langle p\rangle(t)$ and compare with the classical motion. (iv) Show $\Delta x\Delta p=\hbar/2$. (v) Show completeness $\int\frac{d\alpha^*d\alpha}{2\pi i}|\alpha\rangle\langle\alpha|=I$. (vi) Show that $\langle x|\alpha\rangle$ is a Gaussian.

steps.reveal: $a\sum c_n|n\rangle=\sum c_{n+1}\sqrt{n+1}|n\rangle=\alpha\sum c_n|n\rangle$ gives $c_n=\frac{\alpha^n}{\sqrt{n!}}c_0$, i.e. $|\alpha\rangle=c_0e^{\alpha a^\dagger}|0\rangle$; normalisation $|c_0|^2e^{|\alpha|^2}=1$.
$e^{-iHt/\hbar}|n\rangle=e^{-i\omega(n+\frac12)t}|n\rangle$, so $\alpha^n\to(\alpha e^{-i\omega t})^n$ and a global $e^{-i\omega t/2}$: again coherent with $\alpha(t)=\alpha e^{-i\omega t}$.

$x=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{2m\omega}}(a+a^\dagger)$, $p=-i\sqrt{\frac{m\hbar\omega}2}(a-a^\dagger)$: $\langle x\rangle=\sqrt{\frac{2\hbar}{m\omega}}|\alpha|\cos(\omega t-\phi_0)$, $\langle p\rangle=-\sqrt{2m\hbar\omega}|\alpha|\sin(\omega t-\phi_0)$: the classical oscillation (Ehrenfest is exact for the oscillator, $\langle V^\prime(x)\rangle=V^\prime(\langle x\rangle)$).

With $aa^\dagger=a^\dagger a+1$: $\langle x^2\rangle=\frac{\hbar}{2m\omega}(1+2|\alpha|^2+\alpha^2+\bar\alpha^2)$, so $(\Delta x)^2=\frac{\hbar}{2m\omega}$, $(\Delta p)^2=\frac{m\hbar\omega}2$, $\Delta x\Delta p=\hbar/2$ at all times.

Polar coordinates $\alpha=re^{i\theta}$, $d\alpha^*d\alpha=2i\,r\,dr\,d\theta$: the $\theta$ integral gives $2\pi\delta_{nm}$, then $\frac{2}{n!}\int_0^\infty e^{-r^2}r^{2n+1}dr=\frac{\Gamma(n+1)}{n!}=1$: $\sum_n|n\rangle\langle n|=I$.

$\left(\sqrt{\frac{m\omega}{2\hbar}}x+\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{2m\omega}}\frac{d}{dx}\right)\psi_\alpha=\alpha\psi_\alpha$ gives $\psi_\alpha=A\exp\left[-\frac{m\omega}{2\hbar}\left(x-\sqrt{\frac{2\hbar}{m\omega}}\alpha\right)^2\right]$. For $\alpha=0$ it is the ground state, which we already knew is Gaussian.

enc.title: Sheet 7 Q3: Degeneracies

source.where: Exercise sheet VII, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 7.pdf

enc.goal: $D_n^k$ = number of ways to write $n$ as a sum of $k$ non-negative integers; $F^k(s)=\sum_nD_n^ks^n$, $|s|<1$. (i) Show $F^k(s)=\sum_{n_1}\cdots\sum_{n_k}s^{n_1+\dots+n_k}$. (ii) Deduce $F^k=(1-s)^{-k}$ and $D_n^k=\binom{n+k-1}{n}$. (iii) Degeneracies of the isotropic oscillator in 2D and 3D.

steps.reveal: $\prod_j\left(\sum_{n_j}s^{n_j}\right)=\sum_nc_ns^n$ where $c_n$ counts the terms with $n_1+\dots+n_k=n$, i.e. $c_n=D_n^k$.
Each factor is $(1-s)^{-1}$, so $F^k=(1-s)^{-k}=\sum_n\binom{n+k-1}{n}s^n$ (binomial series or $\frac{1}{(k-1)!}\frac{d^{k-1}}{ds^{k-1}}\frac1{1-s}$).

enc.title: Sheet 8 Q1: Angular momentum

source.where: Exercise sheet VIII, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 8.pdf

enc.goal: $\vec L=\vec r\wedge\vec p$, $L_i=\varepsilon_{ijk}r_jp_k$. (i) With $[r_i,p_j]=i\hbar\delta_{ij}$ derive $[L_i,L_j]=i\hbar\varepsilon_{ijk}L_k$ and $[L_3,\vec L^2]=0$. (ii) Evaluate $[L_3,L_1L_2+L_2L_1]$ and deduce $\langle l,m|L_1^2|l,m\rangle=\langle l,m|L_2^2|l,m\rangle=\frac{\hbar^2}2[l(l+1)-m^2]$. Hint: for an eigenstate $|\psi\rangle$ of a self-adjoint $A$, $\langle\psi|[A,B]|\psi\rangle=0$.

steps.reveal: $[L_i,L_j]=\varepsilon_{ikl}\varepsilon_{jmn}[r_kp_l,r_mp_n]=i\hbar(-\varepsilon_{ikl}\varepsilon_{jln}r_kp_n+\varepsilon_{ikl}\varepsilon_{jmk}r_mp_l)$; with $\varepsilon\varepsilon=\delta\delta-\delta\delta$ this is $i\hbar(r_ip_j-r_jp_i)=i\hbar\varepsilon_{ijk}L_k$, since $\varepsilon_{ijk}L_k=r_ip_j-r_jp_i$.
$A|\psi\rangle=a|\psi\rangle$ with $a$ real: $\langle\psi|AB-BA|\psi\rangle=(a-a)\langle\psi|B|\psi\rangle=0$.

$[L_3,L_1L_2+L_2L_1]=2i\hbar(L_2^2-L_1^2)$, so in $|l,m\rangle$: $\langle L_1^2\rangle=\langle L_2^2\rangle$. With $L_1^2+L_2^2=\vec L^2-L_3^2$: each is $\frac{\hbar^2}2[l(l+1)-m^2]$ (and $\langle L_{1,2}\rangle=0$, so these are the variances).

enc.title: Sheet 8 Q2: SO(4)

source.where: Exercise sheet VIII, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 8.pdf

enc.goal: so(4) = tangent vectors at the identity of paths in SO(4). (i) Describe so(4) as a space of matrices. (ii) Find a basis $A_i,B_i$ with $[A_i,A_j]=\varepsilon_{ijk}A_k$, $[B_i,B_j]=\varepsilon_{ijk}A_k$, $[A_i,B_j]=\varepsilon_{ijk}B_k$. (iii) Show so(4) $\cong$ su(2) $\oplus$ su(2).

steps.reveal: $\gamma^T\gamma=I$ gives $\dot\gamma(0)^T+\dot\gamma(0)=0$; conversely $e^{tM}$ for antisymmetric $M$ is in SO(4). So so(4) = real antisymmetric $4\times4$ matrices, 6-dimensional.

$A_i$: rotations in the 3D block $(1,2,3)$, $(A_i)_{jk}=-\varepsilon_{ijk}$ ($A_1$ rotates in the 2-3 plane, etc.); $B_i$: the "boosts" mixing coordinate $i$ with the 4th, $(B_i)_{4i}=1$, $(B_i)_{i4}=-1$. Compute $[A_1,A_2]=A_3$, $[B_1,B_2]=A_3$, $[A_1,B_2]=B_3$, $[A_1,B_3]=-B_2$, $[A_1,B_1]=0$; the rest follows by cyclic permutation of $1,2,3$.

$X_i=\frac12(A_i+B_i)$, $Y_i=\frac12(A_i-B_i)$: $[X_i,X_j]=\varepsilon_{ijk}X_k$, $[Y_i,Y_j]=\varepsilon_{ijk}Y_k$, $[X_i,Y_j]=0$. In hydrogen these are $\frac12(\vec L\pm\vec D)$ built from $\vec L$ and the Runge-Lenz vector: the origin of the $n^2$ degeneracy.

keyPoints: link to $\vec L$ and Runge-Lenz in hydrogen

enc.title: Sheet 8 Q3: Representations of su(2) and the 2D oscillator

source.where: Exercise sheet VIII, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 8.pdf

enc.goal: $J_3=\frac12(a^\dagger a-b^\dagger b)$, $J_+=a^\dagger b$, $J_-=b^\dagger a$. (i) Show $[J_3,J_\pm]=\pm J_\pm$, $[J_+,J_-]=2J_3$. (ii) Show $\vec J^2=\frac N2(\frac N2+1)$, $N=N_a+N_b$. (iii) Give $J_\pm,J_3$ on $|n_a,n_b\rangle$. (iv) With $j=\frac{n_a+n_b}2$, $m=\frac{n_a-n_b}2$ get the standard su(2) form and $|j,m\rangle=\frac{(a^\dagger)^{j+m}(b^\dagger)^{j-m}}{\sqrt{(j+m)!(j-m)!}}|0,0\rangle$. (v) Show the $J$’s commute with $a^\dagger a+b^\dagger b$.

steps.reveal: Using $[a,a^\dagger]=1$ and that $a$’s commute with $b$’s: $2[J_3,J_+]=a^\dagger b+a^\dagger b$, $2[J_3,J_-]=-2b^\dagger a$, $[J_+,J_-]=a^\dagger(1+b^\dagger b)a-b^\dagger(1+a^\dagger a)b=a^\dagger a-b^\dagger b=2J_3$.
$\vec J^2=\frac14(N_a-N_b)^2+\frac12\left(N_a(1+N_b)+N_b(1+N_a)\right)=\frac14(N_a+N_b)^2+\frac12(N_a+N_b)=\frac N2\left(\frac N2+1\right)$.

$J_+|n_a,n_b\rangle=\sqrt{n_b(n_a+1)}|n_a+1,n_b-1\rangle$, $J_-|n_a,n_b\rangle=\sqrt{n_a(n_b+1)}|n_a-1,n_b+1\rangle$, $J_3=\frac12(n_a-n_b)$. With $n_a=j+m$, $n_b=j-m$: $J_\pm|j,m\rangle=\sqrt{j(j+1)-m(m\pm1)}|j,m\pm1\rangle$, $J_3|j,m\rangle=m|j,m\rangle$: the spin-$j$ representation (Schwinger representation).

$[J_+,N_a+N_b]=[a^\dagger,N_a]b+a^\dagger[b,N_b]=-a^\dagger b+a^\dagger b=0$, same for $J_-$, $J_3$. The level $E=\hbar\omega(N+1)$ is the spin $j=N/2$ multiplet: dimension $N+1$, exactly its degeneracy.

enc.title: Sheet 9 Q1: The sech² potential

source.where: Exercise sheet IX, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 9.pdf

enc.goal: $H=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\partial_x^2+V$, $V=-\frac{\hbar^2}{m}\mathrm{sech}^2x$. (i) Sketch $V$ and the expected ground state. (ii) Show $A^\dagger A\psi=(\epsilon+1)\psi$ with $\epsilon=2mE/\hbar^2$, $A=\partial_x+\tanh x$. (iii) Show $\epsilon\ge-1$ and find $\psi_0$ (what is $A\psi_0$?).

steps.reveal: Symmetric well with minimum $-\hbar^2/m$ at $x=0$, going to 0 at $\pm\infty$. Ground state: even, no node, localised in the well, decaying outside.
$A^\dagger=-\partial_x+\tanh x$, $A^\dagger A\psi=-\psi^{\prime\prime}+(\tanh^2x-\tanh^\prime x)\psi=-\psi^{\prime\prime}+(1-2\,\mathrm{sech}^2x)\psi=\frac{2m}{\hbar^2}H\psi+\psi=(\epsilon+1)\psi$.
$\langle\chi|A^\dagger A|\chi\rangle=\|A\chi\|^2\ge0$ gives $\epsilon\ge-1$, saturated when $A\psi_0=0$: $\psi_0^\prime=-\tanh x\,\psi_0$, $\psi_0=\frac{1}{\sqrt2\cosh x}$, $E_0=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}$.

keyPoints: shape of $V$ and an even, nodeless $\psi_0$

enc.title: Sheet 9 Q2: Discreteness of the spectrum

source.where: Exercise sheet IX, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 9.pdf

steps.reveal: A continuum would be summed over a continuum of values with infinite weight: e.g. $V=0$ gives $\int d^dp\,e^{-\beta p^2/2m}\langle p|p\rangle=\infty$ ($\delta(0)$). Rigorously: $e^{-\beta H}$ is then trace class, its spectrum is discrete, hence that of $H$.

$Z\le\int d^dq\,\langle q|e^{-\beta T}|q\rangle e^{-\beta V(q)}$ ($V$ diagonal in $|q\rangle$); inserting momentum states with $\langle q|p\rangle=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}e^{ip\cdot q/\hbar}$: $\langle q|e^{-\beta T}|q\rangle=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d}\int d^dp\,e^{-\beta p^2/2m}$.

Sufficient: $\int d^dq\,e^{- eta V(q)}<\infty$ for all $ eta>0$. For $
u\|q\|^\alpha$: $\mathrm{vol}(S^{d-1})\int_0^\infty r^{d-1}e^{- eta
u r^\alpha}dr= rac{\mathrm{vol}(S^{d-1})}{\alpha( eta
u)^{d/\alpha}}\Gamma( rac d\alpha)<\infty$: discrete (e.g. the oscillator, $\alpha=2$).

enc.title: Sheet 9 Q3: Pauli matrices and rotations

source.where: Exercise sheet IX, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 9.pdf

enc.goal: Show that $U(\omega\vec n)=\exp(-i\frac\omega2\vec n\cdot\vec\sigma)\in SU(2)$ is a rotation by $\omega$ about $\vec n$: (i) $\sigma_j\sigma_k=\delta_{jk}I+i\varepsilon_{jkl}\sigma_l$; (ii) $U=\cos\frac\omega2I-i\sin\frac\omega2\,\vec n\cdot\vec\sigma$; (iii) with $\tilde x=\vec x\cdot\vec\sigma$, compute $\tilde x^\prime=U\tilde xU^\dagger$.

steps.reveal: Check $\sigma_j^2=I$ and $\sigma_1\sigma_2=i\sigma_3$ (cyclic); hence $(\vec x\cdot\vec\sigma)(\vec y\cdot\vec\sigma)=(\vec x\cdot\vec y)I+i(\vec x\times\vec y)\cdot\vec\sigma$ and $(\vec n\cdot\vec\sigma)^2=I$.

Split the series into even powers ($I$) and odd powers ($\vec n\cdot\vec\sigma$): $\cos\frac\omega2I-i\sin\frac\omega2\,\vec n\cdot\vec\sigma$. Note $U(2\pi\vec n)=-I$: spinors change sign under a full turn.

$\tilde x^\prime=\left(\cos\omega\,\vec x-\sin\omega\,\vec x\times\vec n+(1-\cos\omega)(\vec x\cdot\vec n)\vec n\right)\cdot\vec\sigma$: Rodrigues’ formula for a rotation by $\omega$ about $\vec n$ (check with $\vec n=\hat e_3$: $\hat e_1\to\cos\omega\,\hat e_1+\sin\omega\,\hat e_2$).

enc.title: Sheet 9 Q4: 3D oscillator and su(3)

source.where: Exercise sheet IX, Question 4; official solution: Solutions 9.pdf

enc.goal: $H=\hbar\omega(a_1^\dagger a_1+a_2^\dagger a_2+a_3^\dagger a_3+\frac32)$. (i) Show $J_{ij}=a_i^\dagger a_j$ is conserved and $E_{ij}\mapsto J_{ij}$ is a Lie algebra isomorphism from u(3). (ii) For su(3) with $h_1=E_{11}-E_{22}$, $h_2=E_{22}-E_{33}$, $e_1=E_{12}$, $e_2=E_{23}$, $e_3=E_{13}$, $f_i=e_i^T$: compute $\mathrm{ad}_{h_i}$, the roots $\Delta_\pm$, and the su(2) subalgebras. (iii) Highest-weight theory of irreps. (iv) Show that the degenerate eigenspaces of $H$ are su(3) irreps and give their highest weight.

steps.reveal: $[H,a_i^\dagger a_j]=\hbar\omega(a_i^\dagger a_j-a_i^\dagger a_j)=0$. $[E_{ij},E_{kl}]=\delta_{jk}E_{il}-\delta_{il}E_{kj}$ and $[a_i^\dagger a_j,a_k^\dagger a_l]=\delta_{jk}a_i^\dagger a_l-\delta_{il}a_k^\dagger a_j$: the same bracket.

$[h_1,e_1]=2e_1$, $[h_2,e_1]=-e_1$: root $(2,-1)$; $e_2$: $(-1,2)$; $e_3$: $(1,1)$; the $f$’s have the negatives. Each positive root gives $\{e_\alpha,h_\alpha=[e_\alpha,f_\alpha],f_\alpha\}\cong$ su(2) (e.g. $e_3,h_1+h_2,f_3$).

A finite irrep has a weight vector $v$ killed by all $e_\alpha$ (otherwise the weights would grow without bound); $V$ is spanned by the $f$’s acting on $v$. Restricting to each su(2) subalgebra forces $\lambda(h_\alpha)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. The adjoint rep has highest weight vector $e_3$, weight $(1,1)$.

Level $N$ = all $|n_1,n_2,n_3\rangle$ with $\sum n_i=N$, dimension $\frac{(N+1)(N+2)}{2}$. Highest weight vector $(a_1^\dagger)^N|0\rangle$, weight $(N,0)$: the symmetric irrep $\mathrm{Sym}^N(\mathbb C^3)$; su(3) explains the full degeneracy (more than SO(3) alone).

enc.title: Sheet 10 Q1: Harmonic oscillator in spherical coordinates

source.where: Exercise sheet X, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 10.pdf

enc.goal: $H=\frac{\vec p^2}{2m}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}\vec x^2$. (i) Spectrum and degeneracies from what you know. (ii) With $\Psi=\frac{u(r)}rY_{\ell m}$, $-u^{\prime\prime}+\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{r^2}u+\frac{m^2\omega^2}{\hbar^2}r^2u=\varepsilon u$, $\varepsilon=\frac{2mE}{\hbar^2}$: show $u\sim r^{\ell+1}$ ($r\to0$) and $u\sim e^{-m\omega r^2/2\hbar}$ ($r\to\infty$); contrast with hydrogen. (iii) With $u=e^{-m\omega r^2/2\hbar}\sum_{k\ge\ell+1}c_kr^k$ derive $c_{k+2}=\frac{\frac{m\omega}\hbar(2k+1)-\varepsilon}{(k+2)(k+1)-\ell(\ell+1)}c_k$; which $c_k$ vanish, how many are free? (iv) Square integrability: allowed energies at fixed $\ell$; draw the $(\ell,E)$ spectrum. (v) Recover (i).

steps.reveal: $E=\hbar\omega(N+\frac32)$, degeneracy $\frac{(N+1)(N+2)}2$ (sheet VII Q3).

$r\to0$: $u^{\prime\prime}\approx\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{r^2}u$, $u=r^{\ell+1}$ or $r^{-\ell}$; the second is not square integrable (or, for $\ell=0$, would need a $\delta$ potential). $r\to\infty$: $u=e^S$, $S^{\prime2}\approx\alpha^2r^2$, $S=-\alpha r^2/2$ ($\alpha=m\omega/\hbar$). Hydrogen decays only like $e^{-\kappa r}$; here the confining $r^2$ potential gives a Gaussian and no scattering states: the whole spectrum is discrete.

Insert $u=e^{-\alpha r^2/2}f$: $-f^{\prime\prime}+\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{r^2}f+2\alpha rf^\prime+(\alpha-\varepsilon)f=0$; equate powers of $r$: the stated recursion. Starting from $c_{\ell+1}$ in steps of 2, all $c_k$ with $k-\ell$ even vanish; only $c_{\ell+1}$ is free (normalisation).

If the series does not stop, $c_{k+2}/c_k\to2\alpha/k$ and $f\sim e^{\alpha r^2}$: not normalisable. It stops at $k_{\max}=\ell+1+2n_r$ iff $\varepsilon=\alpha(2k_{\max}+1)$, i.e. $E=\hbar\omega\left(2n_r+\ell+\frac32\right)$. In the $(\ell,E)$ plane: at $E=\hbar\omega(N+\frac32)$ the allowed $\ell=N,N-2,\dots,1$ or 0.
$\sum_{\ell=N,N-2,\dots}(2\ell+1)=\frac{(N+1)(N+2)}{2}$: agrees with (i). Same $N$ for different $\ell$: an accidental degeneracy, explained by the hidden su(3) (sheet IX Q4).

enc.title: Sheet 11 Q1: More on the dynamical symmetry

source.where: Exercise sheet XI, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 11.pdf

enc.goal: Pauli-Lenz vector $\vec J=\frac1{2m}(\vec p\wedge\vec L-\vec L\wedge\vec p)-\kappa\frac{\vec x}r$; on a fixed negative energy $\vec S=\frac12(\vec L+a\vec J)$, $\vec D=\frac12(\vec L-a\vec J)$ form su(2) $\oplus$ su(2). (i) The highest weight vector $|\psi\rangle$ (killed by $S_+$, $D_+$) satisfies $J_+|\psi\rangle=L_+|\psi\rangle=0$, so it is a superposition of $|n,l,l\rangle$. (ii) Compute $[L_\pm,J_+]$, $[L_3,J_+]$; show $J_+|n,l,l\rangle\propto|n,l+1,l+1\rangle$ and $|\psi\rangle=|n,n-1,n-1\rangle$. (iii) Check explicitly: $\psi\propto r^{n-1}\sin^{n-1}\theta\,e^{i(n-1)\varphi}e^{-m\kappa r/\hbar^2n}$ and $J_+\psi=0$. (v) Describe the eigenspace with ladder operators and count its dimension.

steps.reveal: $S_+\pm$ and $D_+$ combinations: $S_+|\psi\rangle=D_+|\psi\rangle=0\Leftrightarrow L_+|\psi\rangle=0$ and $J_+|\psi\rangle=0$. $L_+|\psi\rangle=0$ means $m=l$ in each $l$ component: $|\psi\rangle=\sum_lc_l|n,l,l\rangle$.

From $[L_j,J_k]=i\hbar\varepsilon_{jkl}J_l$: $[L_+,J_+]=0$, $[L_3,J_+]=\hbar J_+$, $[L_-,J_+]=-2\hbar J_3$. So $J_+|n,l,l\rangle$ has $L_3=\hbar(l+1)$ and is killed by $L_+$: it is a highest weight of spin $l+1$, $\propto|n,l+1,l+1\rangle$. Then $J_+|\psi\rangle=0$ forces $c_l=0$ unless $l$ is maximal: $|\psi\rangle=|n,n-1,n-1\rangle$.

For $l=n-1$, $u_{n,n-1}\propto r^ne^{-r/na_0}$ (no radial nodes) and $Y_{n-1,n-1}\propto\sin^{n-1}\theta e^{i(n-1)\varphi}$, giving the stated $\psi$ with $\frac{m\kappa}{\hbar^2}=\frac1{a_0}$. With $J_+=\frac im(p_3L_+-\hbar p_+-p_+L_3)-\kappa\sin\theta e^{i\varphi}$ and the given $p_+$, $L_+\psi=0$, $L_3\psi=\hbar(n-1)\psi$, the remaining terms cancel: $J_+\psi=0$.
$|\psi\rangle$ has $S_3=D_3=\frac{n-1}2$: spin $j=\frac{n-1}2$ for both su(2)s. The eigenspace is spanned by $S_-^aD_-^b|\psi\rangle$, $0\le a,b\le n-1$: dimension $(2j+1)^2=n^2$.

enc.title: Sheet 12 Q2: Vectors and tensors

source.where: Exercise sheet XII, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 12.pdf

enc.goal: (i) Show that the so(3) representation of the defining SO(3) action is spin 1 ($M_j=i\frac{d}{d\varphi}R_j(\varphi)|_0$). (ii) Show that $\vec x$ and $\vec p$ transform as vectors under $O\mapsto\hbar^{-1}[L_j,O]$. (iii) Highest and lowest weight components of a vector (spherical basis). (iv) Decompose $S^2D_1$. (v) Combine two vectors $\vec J,\vec K$ symmetrically into a scalar $S$ and a tensor $T$.

steps.reveal: $(M_j)_{kl}=-i\varepsilon_{jkl}$; $M_3$ has eigenvalues $-1,0,1$ and $\vec M^2=2=1(1+1)$: the 3-dimensional irrep $D_1$.
$[L_j,x_k]=i\hbar\varepsilon_{jkl}x_l$, $[L_j,p_k]=i\hbar\varepsilon_{jkl}p_l$: exactly the action of $M_j$ (up to the factor $i$ convention): vector operators.

$S^2D_1$ has dimension 6 $=D_2\oplus D_0$ (a tensor and a scalar; the antisymmetric part would be $D_1$). Scalar $S=\vec J\cdot\vec K$; tensor $T_{ij}=\frac12(J_iK_j+J_jK_i)-\frac13\delta_{ij}\vec J\cdot\vec K$ (symmetric, traceless: 5 components).

enc.title: Sheet 12 Q3: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients

source.where: Exercise sheet XII, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 12.pdf

enc.goal: (i) Prove $\langle l,\frac12,m\mp\frac12,\pm\frac12|l,\frac12,l+\frac12,m\rangle=\sqrt{\frac{l\pm m+\frac12}{2l+1}}$. (ii) For $l=1$ write the states $|j=\frac32,j_z\rangle$ in terms of $|m,s\rangle$.

steps.reveal: $|l+\frac12,l+\frac12\rangle=|l,\uparrow\rangle$ (coefficient 1). Apply $J_-=L_-+S_-$ repeatedly; the recursion relates neighbouring coefficients, $\frac{c(m-1)}{c(m)}=\sqrt{\frac{l+m-\frac12}{l+m+\frac12}}$ for the $\uparrow$ part, which telescopes to $\sqrt{\frac{l+m+\frac12}{2l+1}}$; normalisation (or the other recursion) gives the $\downarrow$ coefficient $\sqrt{\frac{l-m+\frac12}{2l+1}}$.

$|\frac32,\frac32\rangle=|1,\uparrow\rangle$, $|\frac32,\frac12\rangle=\sqrt{\frac23}|0,\uparrow\rangle+\sqrt{\frac13}|1,\downarrow\rangle$, $|\frac32,-\frac12\rangle=\sqrt{\frac13}|-1,\uparrow\rangle+\sqrt{\frac23}|0,\downarrow\rangle$, $|\frac32,-\frac32\rangle=|-1,\downarrow\rangle$ (the $j=\frac12$ states are the orthogonal combinations).

enc.title: Sheet 13 Q1: Time-energy uncertainty

source.where: Exercise sheet XIII, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 13.pdf

enc.goal: (i) Show $\langle\psi|\psi(t)\rangle=\exp\left[-\frac{it}\hbar\langle H\rangle-\frac{t^2}{2\hbar^2}(\Delta H)^2\right](1+O(|t|^3))$. (ii) Show $P[\text{no change}]=\exp(-(\Delta H)^2t^2/\hbar^2)(1+O(|t|^3))$. (iii) What if $|\psi\rangle$ is an eigenstate of $H$?

steps.reveal: $\langle\psi|e^{-iHt/\hbar}|\psi\rangle=1-\frac{it}\hbar\langle H\rangle-\frac{t^2}{2\hbar^2}\langle H^2\rangle+O(t^3)$; the exponential gives the same with $\langle H^2\rangle=(\Delta H)^2+\langle H\rangle^2$.
$|\langle\psi|\psi(t)\rangle|^2$: the phase drops out, $e^{-(\Delta H)^2t^2/\hbar^2}$: the decay time is $\sim\hbar/\Delta H$. For an eigenstate $P=1$ for all $t$, consistent since $\Delta H=0$.

enc.title: Sheet 13 Q2: Quantum Zeno effect

source.where: Exercise sheet XIII, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 13.pdf

enc.goal: $U_t=e^{-iHt/\hbar}$, $P=|\phi\rangle\langle\phi|$. (i) Show $PU_{t/n}P\cdots U_{t/n}P=\langle\phi|U_{t/n}|\phi\rangle^nP$. (ii) Show $\langle\phi|U_{t/n}|\phi\rangle^n=e^{-i\langle H\rangle t/\hbar}(1+O(t^2/n))$. (iii) Deduce the limit $n\to\infty$ and interpret.

steps.reveal: Each $P\,U\,P=|\phi\rangle\langle\phi|U|\phi\rangle\langle\phi|$: $n$ numbers $\langle\phi|U_{t/n}|\phi\rangle$ times $P$.

By Q1, $\langle\phi|U_{t/n}|\phi\rangle=e^{-i\langle H\rangle t/n\hbar}(1+O(t^2/n^2))$; to the power $n$: $(1+O(t^2/n^2))^n=1+O(t^2/n)\to1$. So the limit is $e^{-i\langle H\rangle t/\hbar}P$: continuous measurement freezes the state (watched pot).

enc.title: Sheet 13 Q3: Hardy’s paradox

source.where: Exercise sheet XIII, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 13.pdf

enc.goal: $|\psi\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt3}(|++\rangle+|-+\rangle+|--\rangle)$. Alice measures $A_0$ (basis $|\pm\rangle$) or $A_1$ (basis $|\pm\hat n\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt2}(|+\rangle\pm|-\rangle)$), Bob $B_0$ ($|\pm\rangle$) or $B_1$ ($|+\hat m\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt5}(2|+\rangle+|-\rangle)$, $|-\hat m\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt5}(|+\rangle-2|-\rangle)$). (i) Show $|\psi\rangle\propto|+\hat n\rangle(2|+\rangle+|-\rangle)-|-\hat n\rangle|-\rangle$. (ii) Show $P[a_0>b_0]=P[b_0>a_1]=P[a_1>b_1]=0$. (iii) Classically that implies $P[a_0>b_1]=0$. (iv) Show quantum mechanically $P[a_0>b_1]>0$.

steps.reveal: $|\pm\rangle$ in terms of $|\pm\hat n\rangle$: $|\psi\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt6}\left[|+\hat n\rangle(2|+\rangle+|-\rangle)-|-\hat n\rangle|-\rangle\right]$.
$a_0=+1$ leaves $|++\rangle$: $b_0=+1$ surely. $a_1=-1$ leaves $|-\hat n\rangle|-\rangle$: $b_0=-1$ surely. $a_1=+1$ leaves $|+\hat n\rangle\propto|+\hat n\rangle|+\hat m\rangle$: $b_1=+1$ surely.

Classically $a_0\le b_0\le a_1\le b_1$ always, so $a_0\le b_1$. Quantum: $a_0=+1$ (probability $\frac13$) leaves $|+\rangle$ for Bob, and $|\langle-\hat m|+\rangle|^2=\frac15$: $P[a_0>b_1]=\frac1{15}>0$. The values of non-commuting observables cannot all exist at once (no joint distribution).

keyPoints: post-measurement states for the three zeros

sheets.title: Perturbation theory: anharmonic, Stark, spin-orbit and Zeeman

enc.title: Sheet 14 Q1: Anharmonic oscillator

source.where: Exercise sheet XIV, Question 1; official solution: Solutions 14.pdf

enc.goal: $H=H_0+\lambda(x/x_0)^4$, $x_0=\sqrt{\hbar/m\omega}$. (i) Write $H$ with $a,a^\dagger$. (ii) Matrix elements of $H_a$ and the first-order shift. (iii) Energies to second order in $\lambda$. (iv) Why does perturbation theory fail for large $n$?

steps.reveal: $x/x_0=(a+a^\dagger)/\sqrt2$: $H=\hbar\omega(a^\dagger a+\frac12)+\frac\lambda4(a+a^\dagger)^4$.
Non-zero: $\langle n\pm4|$, $\langle n\pm2|$, $\langle n|$. Normal ordering gives $\langle n|(a+a^\dagger)^4|n\rangle=6n^2+6n+3$: $E^{(1)}_n=\frac{3\lambda}4(2n^2+2n+1)$.

$E_n^{(2)}=\sum_{k=\pm2,\pm4}\frac{|\langle n+k|H_a|n\rangle|^2}{-k\hbar\omega}=-\frac{\lambda^2}{8\hbar\omega}(34n^3+51n^2+59n+21)$; ground state $E_0=\hbar\omega\left[\frac12+\frac34\frac{\lambda}{\hbar\omega}-\frac{21}8\left(\frac{\lambda}{\hbar\omega}\right)^2\right]$.

$E^{(1)}_n/E^{(0)}_n\sim\frac{3\lambda n}{\hbar\omega}$ grows: at large amplitudes $x^4$ dominates $x^2$, so it is no longer a small perturbation (and the series is only asymptotic: for $\lambda<0$ the potential is unbounded).

enc.title: Sheet 14 Q2: Stark effect

source.where: Exercise sheet XIV, Question 2; official solution: Solutions 14.pdf

enc.goal: Hydrogen in a field $\vec E$: $\Delta H=-e\vec E\cdot\vec x$ ($e<0$). Use degenerate perturbation theory for $n=2$: energy shifts and eigenstates to first order.

steps.reveal: Take $\vec E=E\hat z$, $\Delta H=-eEz$. $z$ is odd (parity) and commutes with $L_z$: only $\langle200|z|210\rangle$ survives in the 4-dimensional $n=2$ space.
$\langle200|z|210\rangle=-3a_0$ (radial integral with the given $\Psi_{2,0,0}$, $\Psi_{2,1,0}$).

The $2\times2$ block $\begin{pmatrix}0&3eEa_0\\3eEa_0&0\end{pmatrix}$: $\Delta E=\pm3|e|Ea_0$ for $\frac1{\sqrt2}(|200\rangle\mp|210\rangle)$ (signs depend on the convention for $e$); $|21\pm1\rangle$ unshifted. A linear Stark effect, because of the $\ell$ degeneracy of hydrogen.

enc.title: Sheet 14 Q3: Spin-orbit coupling and Zeeman effect

source.where: Exercise sheet XIV, Question 3; official solution: Solutions 14.pdf

enc.goal: $\Delta H=H_{SO}+H_Z=\frac{1}{2m_e^2c^2}\frac1r\frac{dV}{dr}\vec L\cdot\vec S+\frac{\mu_BB_z}{\hbar}(L_z+2S_z)$. (i) Paschen-Back: $H_Z$ dominates; first-order spin-orbit shift; how large must $B_z$ be? (ii) Both as perturbation: diagonalise the $2\times2$ blocks. (iii) For $B_z=0$ recover spin-orbit; to first order in $B_z$ show $\Delta E=g_{\ell j}\mu_BB_zm_j$ with $g_{\ell,\ell\pm1/2}=\frac{2\ell+1\pm1}{2\ell+1}$.

steps.reveal: Basis $|n\ell mm_s\rangle$: $E=\mu_BB_z(m+2m_s)+\xi_{n\ell}\hbar^2mm_s$, with $\xi_{n\ell}=\frac{e^2}{2m_e^2c^2}\langle r^{-3}\rangle$ and $\langle r^{-3}\rangle=\frac{1}{a_0^3n^3\ell(\ell+\frac12)(\ell+1)}$ (only $L_zS_z$ of $\vec L\cdot\vec S$ has diagonal elements). Valid when $\mu_BB\gg$ fine-structure splitting $\sim\alpha^2\mathrm{Ry}/n^3$: of order a tesla or more.

$[\vec L^2,\Delta H]=[L_z+S_z,\Delta H]=0$: for fixed $\ell$ and $m_j=m+m_s$ only $|m_j-\frac12,\uparrow\rangle$, $|m_j+\frac12,\downarrow\rangle$ mix; diagonalising each $2\times2$ block gives the Breit-Rabi type formulas interpolating between weak and strong field.

$B=0$: $\vec L\cdot\vec S=\frac{\hbar^2}2[j(j+1)-\ell(\ell+1)-\frac34]$. First order in $B$: $\langle L_z+2S_z\rangle=\hbar m_j\left(1+\frac{\langle\vec S\cdot\vec J\rangle}{\hbar^2j(j+1)}\right)$ (projection theorem), giving $g=\frac{2\ell+2}{2\ell+1}$ for $j=\ell+\frac12$ and $\frac{2\ell}{2\ell+1}$ for $j=\ell-\frac12$.
